chunks: And from him, from Salamah, from 'Ali ibn Sayf, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Fudayl ibn [Zayd and] Fudalah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever is mentioned in his presence and his eyes shed tears, Allah has made his face haram (impermissible) for the Fire.

key_terms.حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ وَجْهَهُ عَلَى النَّارِ: Allah made his face haram for the Fire (i.e., he will not enter Hell)
key_terms.ذُكِرْنَا: We are mentioned (referring to the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for shedding tears when the Imams are mentioned?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) to emphasize the eschatological significance of visceral emotional response (tears) during the remembrance of the Ahl al-Bayt. This specific reward—protection from Hellfire by having one's face forbidden from entering it—underscores the Shia theological view that love for the Imams is not merely sentimental but a decisive factor in salvation. The narration links the physical act of weeping to a permanent spiritual state, reinforcing the concept of 'Wala' (divine affinity) as a shield against divine punishment.
